sentences.ko: 이제 너희 다 내 손바닥 안이야.
sentences.text: I got you all right where I want you.

alts.text: Gotcha right where I want ya.
Now all of you are exactly where I want you to be.

sentences.note: **right where I want you** 는 상대가 내 계획대로 딱 걸려들었을 때 씁니다. 게임에서 이기기 직전이나 장난칠 때 으스대며 하는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 아니, 케이크 망칠 거였으면 그냥 내가 구웠지.
sentences.text: All right, IF I WANTED THIS CAKE to be a disaster, I WOULD HAVE BAKED IT MYSELF.

alts.text: Wanted a disaster cake? Coulda baked it myself.
Had I wanted this cake to be a disaster, I would have baked it myself.

sentences.note: 'If I wanted ~, **I would have baked it myself**' 꼴로, 남에게 맡긴 일이 엉망일 때 '그럴 거면 내가 했지' 하고 비꼬는 말입니다. baked 자리에 다른 동사를 넣어 어디든 쓸 수 있어요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리 중에 누구도 다시는 예전처럼 못 살 것 같아.
sentences.text: I don't think any of our lives are ever going to be the same ever again.

alts.text: Nothing's ever gonna be the same for us again.
It seems to me that none of our lives will ever be the same again.

sentences.note: **ever be the same** 은 큰일을 겪고 나서 '이제 예전으로는 못 돌아간다'고 할 때 씁니다. 결혼, 아이 탄생, 이사처럼 삶이 확 바뀐 자리에서 자주 나와요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 국물에 닭도 안 들어갔으니까 그냥 면 삶은 물이네.
sentences.text: And there's no chicken in the broth either, so it's really just noodle water.

alts.text: No chicken in the broth? That's basically noodle water.
There is no chicken in the broth either, so it is really only noodle water.

sentences.note: **really just** 는 '말이 그렇지 결국 ~일 뿐'이라고 깎아내릴 때 씁니다. 음식이나 물건이 이름값을 못 할 때 농담처럼 하기 좋아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 이렇게 운이 좋다니 믿기지가 않아.
sentences.text: And I can't believe how lucky I am.

alts.text: I truly cannot believe how fortunate I am.

sentences.note: **can't believe how lucky I am** 은 고마운 사람이나 좋은 일 앞에서 진심을 담아 하는 말입니다. 결혼식 건배사나 생일 자리에서 흔히 들려요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 오늘 이렇게 여기 서 보니까, 나한테 필요한 건 이미 다 가졌다는 걸 알겠어.
sentences.text: But now I'm standing here today knowing that I have everything I'm ever going to need.

alts.text: Turns out I've already got everything I'll ever need.
Standing here today, I realize that I already have everything I will ever need.

sentences.note: **everything I'm ever going to need** 는 축사나 고마움을 전하는 자리에서 '더 바랄 게 없다'고 말할 때 씁니다. **ever** 가 들어가서 '앞으로 살면서 언제라도'라는 느낌이 붙습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그리고 너 안 하면 편이 안 맞아서 다들 너한테 화낼걸.
sentences.text: And if you don't play, everyone will be mad at you cuz the teams won't be even.

alts.text: Skip it and the teams are uneven, so everyone's gonna be mad.
Should you decide not to play, everyone will be upset with you because the teams will not be even.

sentences.note: **the teams won't be even** 은 게임이나 운동에서 인원수가 안 맞을 때 하는 말입니다. 누구한테 화가 났는지 말할 때는 **be mad at you** 처럼 at 을 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 자, 그럼 난 이만 실례할게. 데이트가 있어서.
sentences.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a date.

alts.text: Gotta run, I've got a date.
Please excuse me, as I have a date.

sentences.note: **if you'll excuse me** 는 대화를 끊고 자리를 뜰 때 정중하게 양해를 구하는 말입니다. 살짝 으스대며 나갈 때도 잘 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 남의 신용카드를 훔칠 정도면, 이미 겁이고 뭐고 다 내다 버린 사람 아니야?
sentences.text: I think when somebody steals your credit card, they've kind of already thrown caution to the wind.

alts.text: Anyone who steals a credit card isn't exactly playing it safe.
I believe that a person who steals your credit card has already thrown caution to the wind.

sentences.note: **thrown caution to the wind** 는 앞뒤 안 재고 위험을 무릅쓸 때 씁니다. **kind of** 를 넣으면 단정하는 말투가 살짝 누그러집니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends
